name: CA-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Pete Aguilar running with a large cash advantage ($3.5M on hand)
District leans Democratic by 7 points on the PVI
Prediction markets price Aguilar at ~95% to win
Republican challenger Stephanie Vargas has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: Aguilar is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Democratic, and markets price his reelection around 95%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the fundamentals-based margin of about 20 points stands with only minor adjustment.
model.watch: Any late surge in challenger fundraising or outside spending against Aguilar would be the first sign the race is competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pete Aguilar, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Southern California district that voted about seven points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles. He enters the general election with roughly $3.5 million on hand after raising $4.7 million, while Republican Stephanie Vargas reports no fundraising totals. No outside groups are spending against Aguilar, and prediction markets give him about a 95 percent chance of winning.

With no public general-election polls and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. Those point to a comfortable Aguilar victory, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
